hypotheses.title: Model-ranked 100-300 m offset-scarp annulus (narrow H27-10 test)
layers: Existing 32-feature matrix, including lidar_lappos_max, lidar_step_max, lidar_ex_max, and lidar_coh100
H28-1 six-band multiscale magnetic/gravity edge matrix
Known-catalogue distance on each spatial holdout and 4-fold OOF ridge probabilities
hypotheses.signature: Reallocate the exact number of H27-4 r1-pruned OOF dots into the 1 < distance <= 3 pixel (100-300 m) annulus around the known catalogue. Rank eligible OOF ridges by the frozen current-best detector probability and preserve the dot budget and >=1.5 px spacing.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: The hypothesis is that an expert-mapped scarp can sit offset from a legacy/catalogue trace, so a LiDAR-supported ridge in a nearby annulus may mark a missing branch or parallel strand. The official Hermant paper reports one local USGS/TLS separation can be up to 400 m; it does not establish a typical 150-400 m distribution or validate this 100-300 m band.
hypotheses.confounders: Catalogue-internal truth is itself the held-out catalogue; the band may merely exploit segmentation proximity. Roads, channels, shorelines, lithologic edges, DEM seams, and broad classifier covariates can mimic scarps. The failed habitat tomography is not used as evidence. No kinematic side-selection is claimed or tested in this narrowed variant.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: H27-4 removes the <=100 m shadow, while no existing rule reallocates that same dot budget to 100-300 m candidates. Unlike the prior draft, this frozen variant tests only the distance annulus using the current-best OOF ranking; it does not claim a mechanically determined side from SLIPSENSE/DIPDIRECT.
hypotheses.cost: low-medium; reuse the prepared matrix, cached H28-1 features, OOF model, and T-v2 candidate code; about one holdout run
hypotheses.data_gate: Hash-pinned prepared features, LiDAR descriptors, and H28-1 edge cache are present locally. No new raw data are needed.
hypotheses.validation: knowledge/03_preregistration_topology_gate.md#addendum-f-h27-10; exact paired comparison to H28-1 + T-v2 + H27-4 r1 on fresh seeds 150-159

hypotheses.title: Add three official GDR 1391 layers that are absent from the detector
layers: Paleo-geothermal sinter/tufa/travertine and altered-bedrock regional vectors
hypotheses.signature: Independent surface and shallow-subsurface thermal/chemical/volcanic evidence for fault-focused fluid flow and young deformation; test each layer family separately before any combination.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: A permeable fault can localize hydrothermal alteration, thermal anomalies, or young volcanic alignments even where no Quaternary surface trace is catalogued.
hypotheses.confounders: Sampling density, groundwater transport, non-fault heat sources, volcanic contacts unrelated to the target fault, and the fact that prior thermal-point-distance features were nearly null.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: The checkout currently holds 21 vent points and 27,092 well/spring rows, but not these regional paleo-geothermal features, 2 m probes, or volcanics polygons. The existing thermal-distance feature arm was measured near zero; this tests new records and polygon geometry instead.
hypotheses.cost: medium-high; external fetch is automated, but requires verified vector reading, fold-safe rasterization, and separate feature arms
hypotheses.data_gate: Official GDR #1391 lists the packages. Exact ZIPs are hash-pinned by a sibling independent runner (2026-09-30); raw files are not in this checkout, and the last workflow-dispatch attempt returned 403. Re-fetch and verify all hashes before use.
hypotheses.validation: After raw-data inventory, preregister a separate spatial holdout with unused seeds; do not reuse 150-159 or treat catalogue-holdout success as a live score.
hypotheses.status: UNTRIED; source packages are not yet present in this checkout.

hypotheses.title: Dilatational-strain and conductivity intersection corridors
hypotheses.signature: Narrow, spatially coincident strain-gradient and conductivity corridors, rather than a high-value threshold on either raster alone.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: A buried active or fluid-bearing strand may have weak surface relief but express local strain concentration and conductive alteration at depth.
hypotheses.confounders: Broad basin conductivity, clay caps, regional strain smoothness, source-depth mismatch, and the fact that a strain anomaly is not a fault trace.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: The current detector uses these layers as scalar channels; no in-repo rule tests their spatial conjunction as a candidate corridor. It is distinct from refuted scalar thermal/radiometric arms and from endpoint graph links.
hypotheses.cost: low-medium; existing raster layers only, but a fold-safe joint-feature definition needs preregistration
hypotheses.data_gate: All listed bands are in the locally restored hash-pinned training-feature mirror.
hypotheses.validation: No run registered yet; reserve fresh seeds after H27-10 and preregister the exact transform, controls, and gate first.

hypotheses.title: Anisotropic seismicity-fabric lineaments
hypotheses.signature: Directional persistence of earthquake-density ridges and their alignment with local shear-rate gradients over scales wider than individual hypocenters.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: A linear earthquake fabric may expose a blind active strand without a clear young surface scarp.
hypotheses.confounders: Aseismic faults, catalog-completeness gradients, earthquake swarms unrelated to a single fault, and over-smoothed density products.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: The source channels were included in the scalar model and channel audit, but no directional seismicity-fabric transform has been tested. It differs from the already refuted oriented LiDAR/geophysics line-integral arm in both signal and physical target.
hypotheses.data_gate: Existing hash-pinned raster bands; no new external data.
hypotheses.validation: No run registered yet; preregister a distinct unused seed range and compare against the current-best holdout baseline.

hypotheses.title: Quality-filtered hydrothermal chemistry gradients, not point-distance buffers
layers: GDR/INGENIOUS wellspring CSV: temp_c, geothermquartz_c, geothermchalc_c, geothermcat_c, thermalclass, station name, and coordinates
Optional H27-16 2 m temperature probes after provenance verification
hypotheses.signature: Quality-controlled, de-duplicated geothermometer/temperature contrasts along short spatial gradients and locally fault-aligned corridors, instead of isotropic distance-to-point surfaces.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: A chemically distinct upflow zone can reveal permeable fault pathways where the surface trace is absent; the target is the spatial contrast and alignment, not proximity to a spring by itself.
hypotheses.confounders: Duplicate sampling, geothermometer validity, groundwater flow away from the fault, sparse biased stations, and non-fault heat sources.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: H27-12 tested simple well/spring distance features and found nearly zero benefit. This candidate instead uses screened measurement values and local contrasts; that distinct transform remains untried and must not be represented as already supported.
hypotheses.cost: medium; point QA/deduplication and fold-safe spatial encoding
hypotheses.data_gate: The in-footprint wellspring CSV is present as an owner-repository mirror; its official GDR package listing is verified, but this session did not independently fetch or re-hash the raw GDR binary.
hypotheses.validation: No run registered yet; preregister quality filters and spatial holdout before feature construction.
hypotheses.status: UNTRIED; separate from the refuted distance-only feature arm.
